question: Where can I get the list of grid connection requests in Germany, with project, technology, capacity (MW), connection node, status and date?

answer.summary: Germany publishes no open nationwide list of grid connection requests; applications (Netzanschlussbegehren) are tracked bilaterally per applicant. Under § 9 KraftNAV, >=110 kV operators keep a joint Kraftwerksanschluss-Register (via BDEW) for >=100 MW generation (excluding storage since 2025-12-23), restricted to eligible applicants and authorities; only TenneT posted an open 2020-02-18 PDF (93 entries: 8 requests, 8 commitments) lacking request dates. Current 2025-2026 releases (BNetzA/SMARD battery survey, 50Hertz 75-node API) give only aggregates where DSO respondent counts, net/gross MW basis and bidirectional storage double-counting must be inferred.
main_caveats: No open request queue exists: under EnWG § 17, EU Reg. 2019/943 Art. 50(4a) and BT-Drs. 21/7866 (§ 17d EnWG-E), operators report request status bilaterally to applicants, not in a public register.

§ 9 KraftNAV covers only generation >=100 MW at >=110 kV for eligible applicants/regulators, and since 2025-12-23 (BGBl. 2025 I Nr. 368) expressly excludes battery storage, where most new queue volume sits.

SMARD counted 18,158 new battery requests in 2025 (573.5 GW, including duplicates by project). Of these, 1,468 received offers in 2025 (33.9 GW). The 1,937 offers issued in 2025 (54.2 GW) also include older requests.

BNetzA/SMARD omits the DSO respondent count and net/gross MW basis; cross-checking Monitoringbericht 2026 p. 96 implies 4 TSOs and up to 813 of 851 DSOs reported in 2025, not all 842 DSOs registered in 2026.

50Hertz's live 75-node API sums requestedGenerationCapacityMw (59.8 GW) and requestedLoadCapacityMw (67.7 GW); both match at 40 nodes, implying bidirectional storage is counted in both (summing to 128 GW double-counts).
answer.confidence_reason: Verified directly in EnWG, KraftNAV (incl. 2025-12-23 amendment), MaStRV, BT-Drs. 21/7866, EU 2024/1747 & 2024/1711, BNetzA/SMARD, all 4 TSOs, VNBdigital, GovData, GridChecker, and 10 sampled DSOs.

attributes.note: TenneT's 2020 KraftNAV PDF names >=100 MW generation projects/operators in its zone; the live § 9 KraftNAV register is restricted and non-KraftNAV queues are unpublished.
attributes.gap_note: Under § 9 Satz 3 KraftNAV, the live joint Kraftwerksanschluss-Register (>=100 MW generation at >=110 kV) is disclosed only to eligible applicants (Anschlussnehmer) and regulatory/supervisory authorities. Connection requests for battery storage (excluded from KraftNAV since 2025-12-23), demand (data centres, electrolysers, industry), plants <100 MW, and <110 kV distribution grids are handled bilaterally and not published as project lists by BNetzA, the 4 TSOs, or sampled DSOs.

attributes.note: TenneT's 2020 KraftNAV PDF lists Primärenergieträger per >=100 MW entry; live § 9 KraftNAV access is restricted and storage/demand/DSO request technologies are unpublished.
attributes.gap_note: TenneT's static 2020-02-18 KraftNAV register reports Primärenergieträger (Erdgas, Steinkohle, Wind offshore, Pumpspeicher, Kernkraft) for >=100 MW generation in its zone. Live access to the BDEW-coordinated § 9 KraftNAV register is restricted to Anschlussnehmer and authorities, and neither BNetzA nor TSOs/sampled DSOs publish per-request technology records for battery storage, renewables <100 MW, or large loads.

attributes.note: TenneT's 2020 PDF reports gross Nennleistung in MW (brutto) per >=100 MW entry; live § 9 KraftNAV data are restricted and 2025-2026 releases give only node or national sums.
attributes.gap_note: Individual requested MW is public only in TenneT's frozen 2020-02-18 KraftNAV PDF (>=100 MW gross generation) and restricted in the live § 9 KraftNAV register. Current 2025-2026 public sources (50Hertz's 75-substation JSON API and BNetzA/SMARD battery surveys) publish only substation-summed or national GW aggregates, and BNetzA § 31 EnWG dispute decisions redact requested MW as business secrets.

attributes.note: TenneT's 2020 PDF names Netzanschlusspunkt (UW) per >=100 MW entry without flagging requested vs assigned; live § 9 KraftNAV is restricted and other queues omit per-request nodes.
attributes.gap_note: TenneT's 2020-02-18 PDF lists a substation, offshore platform, or area (e.g. UW Simbach, OSS Austerngrund, Raum Stade) without explicitly flagging requested versus operator-assigned nodes. Live § 9 KraftNAV site/grid data are restricted to Anschlussnehmer and authorities; 50Hertz's public JSON API reports only summed MW per substation, while Amprion, TransnetBW, TenneT, and sampled DSOs publish no per-request node assignments.

attributes.note: TenneT's 2020 PDF codes request/commitment/expired stages without queue rank; live § 9 KraftNAV is restricted and TSO/DSO queue or Reifegrad scores are bilateral only.
attributes.gap_note: TenneT's 2020-02-18 PDF distinguishes 4 Anschussbegehren [sic], 5 Anschlusszusage, and 6 Begehren/Zusage aufgegeben oder verfallen, but omits queue rank. Live § 9 KraftNAV entries are restricted; under EnWG § 17, EU Reg. 2019/943 Art. 50(4a), and the 4-TSO Reifegradverfahren (launched 2026-04-01), processing status and queue/maturity ranks are communicated bilaterally to each applicant.

attributes.note: No public German source gives application, acceptance or commitment dates per request; TenneT's 2020 KraftNAV PDF leaves erste Einspeisung blank for all pending/committed rows.
attributes.gap_note: Checked § 9 KraftNAV, TenneT's 2020-02-18 Kraftwerksanschlussregister PDF (which includes only an erste Einspeisung column for operating plants and omits application/commitment dates on all status 4 and 5 rows), BNetzA/SMARD, all 4 TSOs, and 10 sampled DSOs. Request and decision dates surface only for single disputed projects in BNetzA § 31 EnWG rulings or municipal B-Plan filings.

attributes.note: Public request-level data stop at TenneT's 2020-02-18 KraftNAV PDF (6+ years stale); current § 9 KraftNAV records are restricted and 2025-2026 public releases are aggregates.
attributes.gap_note: No current public request-level release exists on BNetzA, TSO, or sampled DSO portals as of 2026-11-26; TenneT's open PDF is dated 2020-02-18, whereas current § 9 KraftNAV records (>=100 MW generation excluding storage) are restricted to eligible applicants and authorities.

attributes.note: Only a single frozen 2020-02-18 PDF snapshot from TenneT was found; neither BNetzA nor grid operators publish historical archives of itemized connection-request records.
attributes.gap_note: Checked BNetzA, SMARD, netztransparenz.de, all 4 TSOs, GovData, Capacitypedia, and GridChecker. TenneT exposes only one static 2020-02-18 PDF; SMARD (2024-2026) and GridChecker (Oct 2024-Nov 2026) archive only national or substation-level MW aggregates, not request-level histories.

attributes.note: Neither § 9 KraftNAV nor TenneT states an update schedule for request-level registers, and TenneT's open PDF has not been refreshed since 2020-02-18.
attributes.gap_note: § 9 KraftNAV defines no publication cadence for the Kraftwerksanschluss-Register. Monthly map updates (Art. 50(4a) Reg. (EU) 2019/943; § 17c EnWG-E) and 10-month 4-TSO Reifegradverfahren cycles cover hosting capacity, while at-least-quarterly request status updates go bilaterally to applicants rather than a public list.

sources.name: Kraftwerksanschlussregister der Netzbetreiber nach § 9 KraftNAV (TenneT TSO GmbH)
sources.summary: Static 2020-02-18 PDF extract of TenneT Germany's § 9 KraftNAV power-plant connection register (>=100 MW generation at >=110 kV).
sources.coverage_note: 93 register entries in TenneT's German zone: 8 pending connection requests (3,101 MW), 8 connection commitments (3,327 MW), 23 expired/withdrawn requests, 35 operating, 14 retired/mothballed, and 5 reserve units.
caveats: Frozen at 2020-02-18 with no request or commitment dates; covers only >=100 MW generation in TenneT's zone.
Status 4 is misspelled '4 Anschussbegehren' in the PDF, and capacities include strings like '2 x 480'.

problems: TenneT's current customer landing page on www.tennet.eu returns HTTP 403 (Cloudflare challenge) to automated HTTP clients, whereas the legacy netztransparenz.tennet.eu file host serves the 2020 PDF with HTTP 200.

example.example_request: curl -sL --max-time 60 -o /tmp/tennet_kw_register.pdf "https://netztransparenz.tennet.eu/fileadmin/user_upload/The_Electricity_Market/German_Market/Grid_customers/kraftnav/2020-02_18_TTG_7555_KW-Register.pdf" && pdftotext -layout /tmp/tennet_kw_register.pdf - | grep -E "4 Ansch|5 Anschlusszusage" | head -n 2 | sed -E "s/  +/ | /g"

sources.name: Gemeinsames Kraftwerksanschluss-Register nach § 9 KraftNAV
sources.publisher: German >=110 kV electricity network operators (coordinated via BDEW Bundesverband der Energie- und Wasserwirtschaft e.V.)
sources.format: Operator/BDEW register disclosure upon eligible applicant or authority request (format not publicly standardized)
sources.license: Restricted statutory disclosure (§ 9 Satz 3 KraftNAV; § 5 Abs. 4 KraftNAV confidentiality rules for network model data)
sources.summary: Statutory joint register of >=100 MW generation plants and formal connection requests at >=110 kV across Germany under § 9 KraftNAV, coordinated via BDEW.
sources.coverage_note: Covers >=110 kV operators within Germany's 846 registered electricity network operators (4 TSOs + 842 DSOs in 2026; 14 tested); restricted to eligible >=100 MW generation applicants and authorities.
caveats: Not open to the general public (§ 9 Satz 3 KraftNAV) and excludes all energy storage since 2025-12-23, demand, <100 MW plants, and <110 kV grids.
Operator KraftNAV webpages publish § 3 forms and schematic maps rather than the § 9 register itself.

problems: Statutory access restriction under § 9 Satz 3 KraftNAV limits disclosure of the live register to eligible >=100 MW generation applicants (Anschlussnehmer) and regulatory/supervisory authorities; three sampled DSO portals (Bayernwerk, Westnetz, E.DIS) also block automated HTTP clients with HTTP 403.

members_summary.scope_note: Universe comprises all 4 control-area TSOs and 842 electricity DSOs registered with BNetzA in 2026 (Monitoringbericht 2026, Table 21, p. 97; only operators of >=110 kV networks fall under KraftNAV § 2 Nr. 3). All 4 TSOs and 10 major/regional DSOs across Germany were tested; only TenneT exposed an open (2020) § 9 register PDF, while none published a current itemized request list.
members_summary.pattern: On operator portals (discoverable via vnbdigital.de), check 'Netzanschluss' -> 'Kraftwerk ab 100 MW' or 'Veröffentlichungspflichten' -> 'KraftNAV'; public pages normally contain only § 3 Abs. 1 forms, model contracts, and schematic maps, while request submission/tracking sits behind digital 'Einspeiseportal' / 'Netzanschlussportal' logins.

if_unstructured.summary: Because current per-request queues are confidential, individual connection requests and commitments can only be reconstructed piecemeal from BNetzA § 31 EnWG dispute decisions, municipal Bebauungsplan / UVP permitting dossiers near substations, and Bundestag parliamentary inquiries (for regional/policy aggregates).

local_terms.meaning: Formal grid connection request under § 8 EEG, § 17 EnWG, or § 3 Abs. 2 KraftNAV
Grid connection applications/inquiries (term used on TenneT, 50Hertz, and BNetzA battery-survey pages)
Joint operator register of >=100 MW power plants and connection requests at >=110 kV under § 9 KraftNAV
Grid connection commitment reserving capacity at a connection point (distinct from an unapproved request)
Maturity-based TSO connection-allocation procedure launched 2026-04-01 for storage and large loads, replacing first-come-first-served
Grid connection point / substation assigned or assessed for an installation
BNetzA Beschlusskammer 6 dispute proceeding reviewing rejected or delayed grid connection requests
Multiple parallel connection requests filed across nodes/operators for the same project, inflating aggregate queue totals
